description: Twenty BC fire seasons: 3,286 historical fire perimeters of 10 hectares or more, 2006-2025, totalling 10,928,804 hectares. Each entry is [lon, lat, size_ha, year, source_vertices, ring|null], where lon/lat is the shoelace centroid of the fire's largest ring and the simplified ring itself is kept for the 615 fires of 1,000 ha or more. The input to research/analysis/water-availability.js, which asks what fraction of real fires have an adequate water source in range (docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #13).

notes: Regenerate with: python3 pipeline/firehistory.py data/fire-history-bc.json (about 25 seconds; the WFS is paged 1,000 features at a time). Modifications: fires of 10 ha or more from 2006 onward only; geometry requested at maxAllowableOffset 0.001 degrees (~110 m) and outer rings further Douglas-Peucker simplified at 0.002 degrees before storage; all coordinates rounded to 4 decimal places, about 11 m. PERIMETER LENGTHS COMPUTED FROM THESE RINGS ARE LOWER BOUNDS, because simplification shortens a convoluted edge. The 10 ha floor excludes the thousands of small starts BCWS records each year that are out before anything flies; 2006 is the floor because the perimeter record is thin before it and the capture method changed. Size is the final mapped footprint, not the size on any particular day. The Information was modified. The Province of British Columbia does not endorse this project and nothing here has official status.
